subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should the browser tool make compact goal-shaped reads and post-action change signals the default interaction contract, or keep the current capped snapshot behavior with opt-in efficient mode?
rationale: The remaining work changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility with existing full snapshot workflows, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
options.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while keeping explicit full/raw snapshot access.

options.title: Keep capped snapshots
options.body: Retain current AI snapshot caps and opt-in efficient mode, and treat additional compaction as future targeted improvements.

options.title: Defer to broader context work
options.body: Track this under broader context-budget architecture if maintainers do not want browser-specific defaults.

recommendation.title: Adopt compact browser defaults
recommendation.body: Make compact, goal-shaped reads and small post-action change signals the default while keeping explicit full/raw snapshot access.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about the browser plugin's public model-facing contract, and history points to steipete for snapshot defaults, plugin boundary, and docs ownership.
